instantiated_cells.justification: Section 101.73(A) requires each employer to file, with the updated registration statement, a statement of expenditures (i.e., the principal’s periodic spending report).

Section 101.72(B) requires updated registration statements (with expenditure statements) to be filed by the last day of January, May, and September each year, which is three times per year (triannual).
The statute specifies filing by the last day of January, May, and September (three times yearly) rather than once per year.
The only periodic filing dates stated are the last day of January, May, and September, not monthly.
Because filings are due three times per year (Jan/May/Sep) rather than four times per year, the cadence is not quarterly.
The statute requires three filings per year (Jan/May/Sep), not two per year as semiannual would imply.
Section 101.72(B) specifies a triannual schedule (Jan/May/Sep) and does not set any additional or alternative periodic cadence.
Section 101.73(C) requires an employer’s statement to show the total amount of expenditures made by the employer during the period covered.
Section 101.73(C) provides that 'expenditures' for employer reporting do not include compensation paid to legislative agents, so compensation is not required to be reported.
Section 101.73(C) excludes 'expenses of maintaining office facilities' from the employer’s reportable expenditures, so indirect/overhead costs are not required.

Expenditure is defined to include gifts and items such as food and beverages, entertainment, lodging, and transportation (§101.70(D)(1)), and §101.73(B)(2) requires reporting details when such expenditures are made for covered officials.

The statute requires detailed disclosure for expenditures to particular officials (name, amount, description, date, legislation/client) under §101.73(B)(2), indicating an itemized reporting format rather than only aggregate totals.
Section 101.72(B) requires the updated registration statement filed with the expenditure statement to list the specific bills or resolutions on which the agent actively advocated during the period.

The initial registration requires only a brief description of the type of legislation (§101.72(A)(3)), while periodic updated filings require listing specific bills/resolutions (§101.72(B)) rather than general issue descriptions.

The initial registration statement (part of the employer’s filings) must include the employer’s name and business address (and real party in interest if different), providing principal contact information.

Section 101.72(C) requires an employer’s updated registration statement to contain the required information for all legislative agents engaged by the employer, which necessarily includes identifying the agents.

The registration information required includes each legislative agent’s 'business address' (§101.72(A)(1)), and §101.72(C) requires the employer’s updated statement to include required information for all engaged agents.
Section 101.72(C) contemplates that an employer’s updated registration statement covers all legislative agents engaged by the employer, thereby listing lobbyists employed.
The required employer/agent registration and related expenditure reporting items include names/addresses/occupation and type of legislation, but do not require stating the employer’s business nature.
The filings require listing specific bills/resolutions and reporting expenditures, but do not require reporting the contacts made or communications with officials.
Sections 101.72 through 101.74 set out registration, expenditures, and financial transaction disclosures and contain no requirement to disclose major financial contributors to the employer.
